ETNProject / Co-created by Kunal Chaudhary & Jatin DhimanA TWO-SYSTEM CHAT EXPERIMENT ✳
THE NETWORK, EXPLAINED

Two browsers.
One shared experiment.

YOUR BROWSER⇄PARTNER’S BROWSER

1. Find each other. The free PeerJS signaling service exchanges connection details. Your room code identifies the hosting browser.

2. Agree on the cipher. Both people enter the same cipher and key. A digest checks that the settings match. The key stays in the browser.

3. Exchange messages. The browser substitutes your text, sends ciphertext over a reliable WebRTC data channel, then reverses the substitution at the other end.

4. Watch it work. Click a message to see its plaintext, ciphertext, character mapping, and transmitted JSON. An acknowledgment confirms receipt.

WebRTC uses SCTP over DTLS, normally over UDP. This is a real browser-to-browser networking project, not the earlier Python TCP-socket version. Signaling needs internet; restrictive networks can block peer connections. These classical ciphers are easy to break.
